$comment: Bootstrap kit manifest. Lists CANONICAL repository-relative source paths. Contains references, never content. DELIVERY: source-linked is the ONLY mode this kit offers - a validated canonical source is a PRECONDITION, not a branch, and a run without one FAILS CLOSED with zero target-repository writes. Packaged-snapshot delivery is DEFERRED IN FULL to `add-specboot-packaged-snapshot-delivery`; the `entries` payload->target mapping and the pack-time assembly below are RETAINED AS INSTALLER MACHINERY for that deferred change and are read by no current run. The kit is CLIENT-AGNOSTIC and SOURCE-AGNOSTIC: it carries every client recipe but provisions only the explicitly selected one, and it assumes no particular canonical source location - the source is runtime input, and the resolved path is recorded in NO committed artifact.

entryPoint.$comment: The kit's single entry point. An adoption starts by running this prompt as ordinary prompt text from the target repository; it needs no command infrastructure, no installed package, and no prior configuration there. It asks for a canonical SOURCE, never for a delivery mode.

sourceResolution.$comment: Source location is RUNTIME INPUT. No path is recorded here or in any other canonical artifact, and no COMMITTED artifact records the resolved path either - not the manifest, not the run log, not the handoff prompt. A resolved path lives only in ignored .specboot/local/ state, which ADOPT-18 removes; identity is the checksums. Validation runs before any orchestration instruction is loaded and before the first project write; a failed validation, or no source at all, stops with zero target-repository writes.

requiredArtifacts.note: validated as a READABLE FILE, not merely a present directory - the initial session reads it directly at a source-relative path

modeSelection.$comment: One mode. Absence of a validated source is a REFUSAL, not an alternative route.
modeSelection.source-linked: the delivered mode; entered when a local canonical source is supplied and validates
modeSelection.no-validated-source: FAIL CLOSED - the run stops, reports that a validated canonical source is required, and leaves the target repository byte-for-byte unchanged
modeSelection.packaged-snapshot: DEFERRED to `add-specboot-packaged-snapshot-delivery`. Never selected by a current run; retained as a readable value only so an earlier run's manifest is read as history rather than re-interpreted.

sourceResolution.readOnly: The validated source is read-only for the entire adoption, including for improvement proposals. A step that wrote to it is FAIL.

gitProvenance.$comment: THREE dispositions, never two. A dirty working tree has content that no commit identifies, so recording its HEAD as identity is precisely wrong - worse than absent, because a reader can resolve it, diff nothing, and conclude the source matched. Identity remains the CHECKSUMS in all three cases.
gitProvenance.dirty: worktree 'dirty', status 'unavailable', with its reason; any observed HEAD goes in `observed-head` as labelled context, NEVER in `commit`

payloadRoot.$comment: Belongs to the DEFERRED packaged-snapshot mode. Never created by a source-linked run. Its ignore rule is still provisioned unconditionally as a property of the installer, not as a claim that the mode is available.

entries.purpose: The authoritative adoption contract, readable before SpecBoot is installed.
Conventions, phase files, troubleshooting and the run-log template.
The orchestration skill body that executes the contract.
States what the transient directory is and that ADOPT-18 removes it.

sourceLinkedEntrySet.$comment: THE DELIVERED MODE. Nothing canonical is copied, and .specboot/bootstrap/ is never created. The entries below are the only canonical paths a temporary discovery entry may point at, resolved RELATIVE TO THE RUNTIME-SUPPLIED SOURCE. The external source is never itself a manifest entry, which is what puts it out of reach of every inventory-driven operation.
sourceLinkedEntrySet.payloadTargetMapping: not applicable - no payload is produced or consumed

entryModes.symlink: the discovery entry is a symlink to the external canonical path
entryModes.appended-block: a delimited block in a pre-existing client instruction file, byte-restored at ADOPT-18
entryModes.$noPointerFile: 'pointer-file' is REMOVED. Discovery is a property of the client, not of the filesystem: a real file naming an external path is not a discovered skill and is never recordable as a discovery entry. Where symlinks are unavailable and the selected client's recipe offers no native mechanism without one, the run FAILS CLOSED before provisioning and no entry is written. See discovery/symlink-fallback.md.

sourceLinkedEntrySet.machineLocal: Source-linked discovery entries name an absolute external path and resolve on one machine only. They are excluded from every checkpoint's staged scope, are never committed, and are removed or byte-restored by ADOPT-18.
sourceLinkedEntrySet.debootstrap: ADOPT-18 removes only the project-local entries above. The payload and container obligations are recorded 'SKIPPED - source-linked mode'.

durableArtifacts.purpose: The durable control record. Written by ADOPT-00, updated (never deleted) by ADOPT-18.
The filled run log. The documented resume source.

ignoreRules.$comment: Transient paths are git-ignored PER PATH, by the same git check-ignore probe and conservative fallback. The durable root is NEVER ignored - it holds committed evidence. A broader '.specboot/' pattern is forbidden because it would swallow the durable root. '.specboot/bootstrap/' is provisioned unconditionally even though no current run creates it: the rule is a property of the installer, not a claim that the deferred mode is available.

clientAgnostic.$comment: The kit carries every recipe and provisions one. No kit file assumes a particular client, and no adoption is required to configure or validate more clients than it selected.
clientAgnostic.provisions: only the clients explicitly declared SELECTED at ADOPT-00

sourceAgnostic.$comment: The mirror of clientAgnostic. A kit that hard-codes a source is exactly as broken as one that hard-codes a client.
sourceAgnostic.sourceIs: runtime input supplied by the operator at ADOPT-00
sourceAgnostic.resolvedPathRecordedIn: no committed artifact at all - not the manifest, not the run log, not the handoff prompt. Only machine-local, git-ignored .specboot/local/ state, removed by ADOPT-18.
sourceAgnostic.identityIs: the recorded guide and skill checksums, plus the Git commit where the source is a CLEAN working tree

clientSupport.$comment: Recipe availability, NOT per-adoption status. A recipe existing here says nothing about whether any given adoption selected that client. Per-adoption status (SELECTED+PASS / SELECTED+PENDING EVIDENCE / SELECTED+FAIL / NOT SELECTED) is recorded in that adoption's run log, never here. Support is evidence-based: a client is never PASS without a fresh-session discovery AND execution test observed by that adoption.

claude.gateEvidence: mechanism matches the relative-symlink convention this repository already uses; each adoption records its own fresh-session PASS

kiro.gateEvidence: mechanism matches the confirmed .kiro/skills convention; project-instruction path is confirmed from the installed version at ADOPT-00; each adoption records its own fresh-session PASS

codex.gateEvidence: gate parts 1-2 complete (official docs 2026-08-12, .agents/skills scan path; isolated scratch repository). Part 3, the fresh-session discovery-and-execution test, NOT observed - see reports/codex-discovery-gate.md. This is a DEFERRED CLIENT-SPECIFIC OBLIGATION: PENDING EVIDENCE as a shipped recipe, carried forward to any adoption that selects Codex. An adoption that did not select Codex records it NOT SELECTED and is not blocked by it.

clientSelection.neverInferredFrom: presence of a client directory on disk
clientSelection.rule: Provision and validate only the recipe(s) for clients declared SELECTED. Every other client is recorded NOT SELECTED.

statusSemantics.NOT SELECTED: nothing provisioned or validated; never blocks; never recorded as PENDING EVIDENCE

clientSelection.passScope: A PASS proves support for the client that produced it and for no other; never universal or multi-client support.
clientSelection.required: An explicit, supported selection is a PRECONDITION of every bootstrap write. No selection at all REFUSES; a selected client with no recipe REFUSES, naming the supported clients. Both refusals precede the preflight and leave the target repository byte-for-byte unchanged. A placeholder such as 'undeclared' is NEVER written to the committed manifest - a committed placeholder is a durable claim that a human made a choice they did not make.

entriesNote: RETAINED INSTALLER MACHINERY for the deferred packaged-snapshot mode. This payload->target mapping and the pack-time assembly that consumes it are kept so the deferred change inherits working drift protection; a source-linked run assembles and consumes NOTHING, so its single-copy guarantee holds trivially and it has no drift surface. No current run reads this mapping.

refusals.$comment: Every refusal happens BEFORE the first write and leaves the target repository byte-for-byte unchanged. A refusal is a clean stop, never a degraded success, and none is resolved by the run choosing on the operator's behalf.

no-source.reports: that a validated canonical source is required, and the three required artifacts

invalid-source.reports: which required artifact or artifacts are missing

no-client-selected.owner: manifest.json#clientSelection.required (canonical rule: ADOPT-00); selection ROUTES are in client-autodiscovery.md
no-client-selected.reports: that an explicit human selection is required

unknown-client.owner: manifest.json#clientSelection.required (canonical rule: ADOPT-00); selection ROUTES are in client-autodiscovery.md
unknown-client.reports: the unsupported client, together with the clients that ARE supported

no-symlink-discovery-unsupported.reports: the client, the discovery mechanism its recipe requires, and what was attempted

preflight.$comment: A complete preflight precedes every write (design D-X). It resolves EVERY target path the selected client's recipe and the durable state will occupy, classifies each, and reports ALL collisions together - discovering them one failed write at a time means the operator approved a mutation set the run already knew was incomplete.
preflight.approvalGate: presents the EXACT mutation inventory: each path, created or modified, by what mechanism, and whether reversible. The run performs exactly that inventory and nothing outside it.
preflight.mechanismChange: A path needing a different mechanism than the one approved requires a NEW gate, never an adjustment.
preflight.onFailure: Provisioning is ALL-OR-NOTHING: a failure restores the pre-provisioning state, leaving no partial discovery entry, manifest, run log, ignore rule, or machine-local store. The end state of a failed bootstrap is a repository that was never bootstrapped.
